paper_metadata.title: Age differences in outcome after mild traumatic brain injury: results from the HeadSMART study

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study provides a clear description of the source population, recruitment setting (two EDs), and specific inclusion criteria (VA/DoD mTBI criteria). Baseline characteristics are well-documented and compared between age groups.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: A sample of 447 adults meeting VA/DoD criteria for mTBI was dichotomized by age into older (≥ 65 years; n=88) and younger (<65 years; n=359) sub-groups.
items.reasoning: The population is clearly defined by age and clinical diagnostic criteria.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: HeadSMART was a prospective cohort study recruiting from two Johns Hopkins emergency departments in Baltimore, MD
items.reasoning: The recruitment setting and prospective nature are explicitly stated.

items.label: Recruitment period
items.prompt: Period of recruitment is adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: Recruitment for HeadSMART occurred between April 2014 and April 2017.
items.reasoning: Specific dates for the recruitment window are provided.

items.label: Place of recruitment
items.prompt: Place of recruitment (setting and geographic location)  are adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: recruiting from two Johns Hopkins emergency departments in Baltimore, MD
items.reasoning: The specific medical centers and city are identified.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: All participants presented to the emergency department within 24 hours of sustaining a head injury... met VA/DoD criteria for mTBI... those with moderate and severe head injury were excluded
items.reasoning: The study uses standardized clinical criteria (VA/DoD) and a specific time-from-injury window.

items.label: Baseline characteristics
items.prompt: The baseline study sample (i.e., individuals entering the study) is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Detailed information on participant characteristics is displayed in Table 1. There were significant differences across age groups for marital status (p ¼ 0.024) as well as employment status, race, and sex (p < 0.001).
items.reasoning: Table 1 provides a comprehensive breakdown of demographics and clinical history.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: There is a notable drop-off from the baseline sample (n=447) to the 6-month follow-up (n=291), representing approximately 35% attrition. While the analysis uses Mixed Effects models to handle missing data, the characteristics of those lost to follow-up are not explicitly compared to completers.

items.reasoning: The follow-up rate at 6 months is roughly 65% (291/447), which is below the preferred 80% threshold for low risk.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study uses validated, standard instruments (GOSE, PHQ-9, RPQ) for TBI outcomes. While the assessments were via telephone/in-person (subjective), they are the gold standard for these constructs.

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: outcomes were assessed at 1-, 3-, and 6-month intervals. Depressive symptoms were assessed using the Patient Health Questionnaire–9 (PHQ-9), post-concussive symptoms (PCS) were ascertained with the Rivermead Post-Concussion Questionnaire (RPQ), and functional recovery from the Extended Glasgow Outcome Scale (GOSE).
items.reasoning: All outcomes and follow-up windows are explicitly defined.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome
items.prompt: The method of outcome measurement used is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and confirmation of outcome with valid and reliable test).
items.evidence_snippet: The Extended Glasgow Outcome Scale (GOSE) (Jennett & Bond, 1975) ascertains an individual's level of functional recovery... PHQ-9... has been found to produce adequate reliability and validity in detecting depression following TBI
items.reasoning: The study uses well-validated scales with citations for their psychometric properties in TBI.

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement

items.evidence_snippet: Outcome data were collected 1-, 3-, and 6-months after enrolment via telephone interview or in-person assessment.
items.reasoning: The protocol was standardized for the whole cohort.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study identifies significant baseline differences between age groups (Mechanism of injury, Sex, Race, Employment) but the primary longitudinal analysis (Mixed effects logistic regression) does not appear to adjust for these confounders. The authors admit this as a limitation.

items.reasoning: While demographics and injury mechanism were measured, several critical geriatric confounders (comorbidities, meds) were missed.

items.evidence_snippet: Longitudinal mixed effects logistic regression models were then estimated to evaluate odds of each outcome over time as a function of age.
items.reasoning: The models described in Table 4 only include Age, Time, and Age*Time. There is no evidence of multivariable adjustment for the significant baseline differences (Sex, Race, Mechanism).
